title: Understanding Janitorial Trip Fees & 2-Hour Night Crew Minimums
seoTitle: Janitorial Trip Fees & 2-Hour Crew Minimums: 2026 US Cost Guide
metaDescription: Janitorial trip fee minimum hours explained: $90–$135 visit floors, 2-hour labor math, and small-suite savings. Run our calculator or compare quotes.
excerpt: Learn why US commercial cleaning contractors enforce $90 to $135 per-visit minimums and 2-hour night crew floors on offices under 1,500 sq ft. Use these labor-hour breakdowns and scope strategies to turn unused dispatch minutes into real facility value.
quickAnswer: Most US commercial cleaning contractors enforce a $90 to $135 minimum per-visit trip fee—typically tied to a 2-hour crew minimum at $35 to $65 per billable hour—regardless of how small your suite is. For offices under roughly 600 to 900 sq ft, this minimum floor overrides the $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft small-suite bracket and pushes effective per-visit rates to $0.18 to $0.28 per sq ft.

blocks.text: Office managers leasing suites between 500 and 1,500 sq ft often experience sticker shock when comparing their first janitorial proposals against national averages. You know the benchmark for small commercial spaces runs **$0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft**, so a 600 sq ft suite with one restroom looks like it should cost around $90 or less—yet legitimate, insured contractors routinely quote **$115 to $145 per visit**.

That gap exists because commercial cleaning is a mobile route business constrained by minimum dispatch economics. Before you negotiate rate cuts or switch to an uninsured independent cleaner, you need to understand how **janitorial trip fee minimum hours** work inside a contractor's payroll model—and how our [Office Cleaning Cost Guides](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/) benchmark small-suite floors across US markets.
Why Commercial Cleaners Enforce a $90–$135 Trip Fee and 2-Hour Minimum

Across the United States, standard recurring commercial cleaning bills at **$35 to $65 per labor hour** (rising to **$55 to $95 per hour** for specialty restoration or biohazard remediation). At those bill rates, dispatching a W-2 technician for a 35-minute cleaning job would generate less than $35 in gross revenue while consuming nearly an hour of unpaid drive time, vehicle wear, and administrative overhead.

Even more important is employee retention. Night-shift custodians rarely accept part-time routes that pay for 45 minutes of clock time between two buildings 20 minutes apart. To guarantee W-2 workers viable shift earnings and cover statutory payroll burden—FICA, unemployment taxes, Workers' Compensation, and General Liability insurance—established contractors set a **$90 to $135 minimum per visit**, which corresponds to roughly **1.5 to 2.0 billable labor hours**.

blocks.title: The Small-Suite Crossover Threshold
blocks.text: Under national pricing benchmarks ($0.12–$0.20 per sq ft for suites under 2,500 sq ft plus $15–$30 per restroom), a 500 sq ft office with one restroom calculates to $80–$138 raw per visit—triggering the $90–$135 minimum floor on the low end. Once your suite reaches 750 to 1,000 sq ft with a restroom, square-footage math clears the trip fee threshold cleanly.
Where Square-Footage Pricing Beats the Minimum Visit Floor

Understanding the crossover point between a flat trip fee and true square-footage pricing prevents you from overpaying—or from shrinking your scope under the false assumption that a smaller cleanable area will automatically lower your bill. If a vendor's minimum visit fee is $120, trimming conference rooms out of your scope inside an 800 sq ft suite produces **zero invoice savings** because you remain pinned to the trip floor.

Using the ISSA commercial production average of roughly **3,500 sq ft per labor hour** (typically **2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr** depending on workstation density) plus **0.15 to 0.25 hours per restroom**, a single custodian finishes a 750 sq ft suite in under 45 active minutes. That leaves paid slack inside a 2-hour minimum window until square footage climbs past 2,000 to 2,500 sq ft.

blocks.text: How Crew Size Multiplies Your Minimum Hours Exposure

A common trap in small-suite proposals happens when a contractor sends a **two-person crew** rather than a solo custodian and applies a 2-hour minimum *per person*—effectively creating a **4-labor-hour minimum** ($140 to $260 per stop) for a suite that only needs 70 minutes of total work. Two-person teams make sense above 4,000 to 5,000 sq ft where one technician pulls trash and cleans restrooms while the second vacuums, or in buildings with tight [downtown parking and freight elevator access fees](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/parking-validation-and-downtown-access-fees/).

For suites under 2,500 sq ft, specify a **solo assigned technician** in your RFP and verify how the vendor bills minimum shifts. Equipped with high-efficiency tools—such as the **Rubbermaid Commercial 36-Inch Cotton Dust Mop Frame & Handle** (36-in head, Swivel 360 maneuverability, 60-in handle) for rapid lobby sweeps, the **Bona Commercial System Multi-Surface Hardwood Mop Kit** (18-in base, telescoping handle, 2 washable microfiber pads, wood-safe construction) for reception plank floors, and **Microfiber Wholesale 16x16 Commercial Cleaning Cloths (150-Pack, Color-Coded)** (150 cloths, 16x16 in, 300 GSM, 4-color OSHA coding separating red restroom, yellow glass, blue general, and green kitchen wipes)—one well-equipped cleaner completes every routine task cleanly within a single 1.5- to 2-hour dispatch.

blocks.title: Beware Sub-$75 Per-Visit Bids on Small Suites
blocks.text: If a bidder quotes $50 to $65 per visit for a commercial office under 1,000 sq ft, verify whether they carry statutory Workers' Compensation and $1M/$2M Commercial General Liability. Quotes below the $90–$135 trip floor often rely on misclassified 1099 contractors or uninsured sole operators who skip restroom disinfection and drop accounts within 60 days.
Extracting Full Value From Paid Minimum Shift Minutes

Once you accept that a **$90 to $135 minimum visit fee** is unavoidable for a small office, the smartest procurement move is capturing the unused labor minutes already built into that floor. Instead of paying a crew for 2 hours when routine vacuuming and trash removal take 50 minutes, assign rotating detail tasks inside your statement of work.

items: **Breakroom & Appliance Detailing:** Fold microwave interior wiping, sink descaling, and fridge-handle sanitization (normally a $12 to $25 per-visit add-on) into the remaining minimum-hour buffer.

**Entry & Conference Glass Spot-Wiping:** Use spare minutes for sidelight and interior glass partitions—which otherwise carry a $15 to $35 per-visit line item—especially in suites with [floor-to-ceiling interior glass partitions](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/how-ceiling-height-and-glass-impact-cleaning-cost/).

**Weekly vs. Twice-Weekly Consolidation:** Shifting from 2x/week (8.66 visits/mo at 1.00x) to 1x/week (4.33 visits/mo at 1.08x) cuts monthly spend nearly in half—from $780–$1,196 down to $390–$598 on a 500 sq ft floor-bound suite—while adding a mid-week team tidy-up.
**Co-Tenant Route Clustering:** Ask your property manager which vendor already services neighboring suites on your floor; shared building access often lets that contractor waive half the trip fee.

blocks.text: Remember to check how your vendor translates weekly frequency into monthly billing. Because a 52-week year averages **4.333 weeks per month**, a 1x/week contract delivers **4.33 visits per month** and a 2x/week contract delivers **8.66 visits per month**. Multiply your quoted monthly retainer by 12 and divide by annual visits to confirm you are not paying a hidden 4-week-month surcharge, or run the exact numbers for your space in our [Office Cleaning Cost Calculator](/office-cleaning-cost-calculator/) and audit competing proposals side by side in the [Quote Comparator](/compare-cleaning-quotes/).
5 Steps to Negotiate or Eliminate Unnecessary Trip Fees

items.name: Identify the Incumbent Building Contractor
items.text: Ask your landlord or property manager which janitorial firm already cleans common hallways or adjacent suites in your building; because their crew is already on site, they can often trim or waive the $15–$25 transit component of a trip fee.

items.name: Lock In a 1-Person Crew Specification
items.text: For suites under 2,500 sq ft, specify a single W-2 technician in your contract so the bidder cannot multiply a 2-hour minimum across two workers.

items.name: Trade Unused Minimum Minutes for Rotating Scope Tasks
items.text: Build a rotating weekly task list—baseboards, breakroom microwave interiors, high-touch door frames, and glass sidelights—so you receive a full 90 to 120 minutes of value inside the $90–$135 minimum charge.

items.name: Test Frequency Before Cutting Square Footage
items.text: Reducing service from 2x/week to 1x/week cuts minimum-fee triggers by 50% per month, whereas removing two private offices from your cleaning map saves $0 if you stay under the visit floor.

items.name: Require Timeclock Logs and a Valid COI
items.text: Insist on geofenced mobile timekeeping or alarm log timestamps alongside a Certificate of Insurance ($1M/$2M GL Additional Insured and Workers' Comp) so a 2-hour minimum actually translates into thorough on-site execution.

faqs.q: What is a standard minimum charge for US commercial office cleaning?
faqs.a: Across most US metro markets, insured commercial cleaning contractors enforce a $90 to $135 minimum charge per visit, which typically reflects 1.5 to 2.0 billable labor hours at $35 to $65 per hour. Even if a 500 sq ft suite only takes 40 minutes to vacuum and sanitize, fixed drive time, alarm check-in, insurance, and minimum shift guarantees keep per-visit pricing at or above that threshold.

faqs.q: At what square footage does a janitorial trip fee stop applying?
faqs.a: At national average rates ($0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft for suites under 2,500 sq ft plus $15 to $30 per restroom), most offices cross above the $90 to $135 minimum visit floor between 700 and 1,000 sq ft. Suites above 1,200 sq ft with one or two restrooms are almost always priced by square footage and restroom count rather than a flat trip fee.

faqs.q: Can I ask a cleaning company for a 1-hour weekly visit instead of a 2-hour minimum?
faqs.a: You can request a 1-hour cap, and some local route cleaners already servicing your office park or downtown building will honor a 1-hour minimum ($55 to $85 per visit) if they can walk directly from another suite. However, stand-alone routes that require a separate vehicle dispatch almost always require a 2-hour minimum to retain W-2 staff and cover Workers' Compensation overhead.

faqs.q: What insurance and OSHA documents are included in a legitimate minimum-fee bid?
faqs.a: Even on a $90 to $135 minimum-visit contract, a compliant US janitorial vendor must provide a Certificate of Insurance showing $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability naming your company as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation coverage, a fidelity bond, and OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) Safety Data Sheets for all on-site chemicals.

faqs.q: How do 4.333 weeks per month affect small-suite monthly retainers?
faqs.a: Commercial contracts average 52 weeks divided by 12 months—4.333 weeks per month—so a weekly (1x/week) trip-fee account bills for 4.33 visits monthly ($390 to $585/month at a $90–$135 floor) rather than 4.00 visits. Always check whether a low monthly quote quietly omits service on the fifth week of five-week calendar months.
